subject: Sprint-to-launch gap closure plan & QBR prep: action items and owners
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: tessa_morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sprint-to-launch gap closure plan & QBR prep: action items and owners

Team —

QBR is next Wednesday and I want to make sure we have a concise, actionable slide and a short risk register to share with execs. Attached are the current worksheets (qbr_risks_v1.xlsx, release_timelines_v3.pdf). I ran a quick gap check across the product/eng epics slated for the July Dedicated launch and flagged the items below that need decisions or immediate mitigation: 

- Telemetry ingestion backlog (EPIC: observability-ingest): missing schema contract with infra; impacts SLO measurement; owner needed.
- Tokenizer upgrade (renderer/tokenizer): the vendor patch introduced a peak-latency regression in internal perf runs — blocker for quantized pipelines.
- Canary gating criteria: we do not have a crisp pass/fail threshold for the first canary (release vs. fallback).
- Feature-cut plan: we need a prioritized list for what to drop if we need to slip date by 2 weeks.

Please reply with: 1) owners for each risk, 2) concrete next step (ticket/POC/roll-back) and 3) target completion date by EOD Monday. I will compile a one-page summary for QBR and circulate.

Also: please review the Release Timeline PDF — the sprint burn on core infra is behind by ~3 story points on average. If that trend continues we need to consider deferring non-critical items.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): qbr_risks_v1.xlsx, release_timelines_v3.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sprint-to-launch gap closure plan & QBR prep: action items and owners

Kimberly — thanks for the sanity check and the attachments. High level notes: 

- Telemetry ingestion backlog: I will own the schema contract. Action: create RFC and run a 2-day design spike with infra. Ticket: ENG-1012 (I will open by EOD Monday). Target: 2027-06-21.

- Tokenizer upgrade: confirmed regression in internal bench. Marcus, can you confirm whether we can pin to previous tokenizer until vendor issue is patched? If not, engineering needs a rollback plan.

- Feature-cut list: Product will send a prioritized list by Monday noon. My initial suggestion is: 1) experimental multi-turn caching, 2) non-essential admin UI widgets, 3) expanded telemetry sampling for cold-starts.

I agree we should be conservative on scope and present a clear fall-back path in the QBR.

-L

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

Cc: marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 11:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sprint-to-launch gap closure plan & QBR prep: action items and owners

Thanks Kimberly — quick escalation from product/ops perspective: the Dedicated launch throughput commitments are in the SLA and sales-committed to two pilot customers (Acme and Nova). If tokenizer or telemetry issues persist, my recommendation is: 

1) Freeze non-essential features and define a "minimum GA" feature set by Monday EOD.
2) Establish canary pass criteria: 99th-pct latency change <= 5% vs baseline; no increase in token drop rate; stable throughput at target load for 30 mins.
3) If canary fails on the first run, trigger alpha-go (limited customer cohort) on July 12 while we fix the regression.

I'd rather present a conservative plan at QBR: scope cut + clear rollback + canary gating. Marcus, engineering will need an extra 48 hours on the testbed for the canary — can you confirm availability?

-Vivek

Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sprint-to-launch gap closure plan & QBR prep: action items and owners

Vivek — we can allocate the testbed for 48 extra hours but it means shifting one scheduled infra migration (we'll reschedule to the following week). Action items from eng: 

- Tokenizer rollback: eng will open ENG-1034 to pin the tokenizer at v2.1.4 and run full quantized perf suite. Owner: Marcus Lin. ETA: 2027-06-18.
- Canary playbook: attached canary_run_playbook.md (small checklist + escalation flow). I'll also assign two on-call engineers for the first run.
- Telemetry contract: will collaborate with Laura on the RFC and provide the ingest pipeline adapters by 2027-06-21.

We will aim for the 5% regression threshold — if the tokenizer pin still shows regressions we will enable the software fall-back (disabled quantization for affected model variants) until vendor patch arrives.

Marcus

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 16:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sprint-to-launch gap closure plan & QBR prep: action items and owners — consolidated

Thank you all for the quick responses and clear owners. Consolidating for the QBR slide and next steps (please treat as the official action tracker):

- Telemetry ingestion contract: Owner = Laura Bennett (ENG-1012). Deliverable: RFC + spike. Target: 2027-06-21.
- Tokenizer regression / rollback: Owner = Marcus Lin (ENG-1034). Action: pin tokenizer to v2.1.4, run quantized perf suite. Target: 2027-06-18.
- Canary gating criteria and run: Owner = Vivek Kulkarni (coordination) + Marcus Lin (execution). Deliverable: canary_run_playbook.md; testbed reserved + 48 hours. Canary pass criteria: 99th-pct latency delta <= 5% and stable throughput for 30 mins. Canary window target: 2027-07-01.
- Feature-cut list: Owner = Laura Bennett. Deliverable: prioritized feature-cut list for scope lock. Target: 2027-06-15 noon.

Kim will assemble the QBR one-pager and the risk slide by Tuesday EOD and circulate for final signoff. If any owner cannot meet the target, flag here immediately so we can adjust the QBR language.

Related links: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1QBR-Prep-Slides, https://redwood.atlassian.net/boards/42?selectedIssue=ENG-998

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
